anti_overlap: fd-dimension-construct-validity covers whether individual dimensions are internally valid
fd-pillar-dimension-gap covers which product pillars are missing from eval coverage
fd-llm-judge-reliability covers how LLM evaluators perform on the rubric
decision_lens: Flags cases where the eval design conflates 'similar to the human reference' with 'editorially good'.
focus: Whether reference-relative scoring is the right evaluation paradigm for line-editing quality
name: fd-reference-relative-scoring
persona: An evaluation methodology researcher who has studied the limitations of reference-based NLG evaluation.
review_areas: Assess whether fidelity and completeness are measuring editorial quality or just reconstruction ability
Evaluate the risk of reference overfitting: models learning to copy the reference rather than apply principles
Check whether the eval distinguishes 'different but equally valid editorial choice' vs 'missed an issue'
Examine whether principle_adherence can surface correct principles applied with different surface choices
Consider whether a dual evaluation (reference-relative + absolute pillar quality) would be better
Review whether the calibration ceiling validates that reference-relative scoring works
success_hints: A model producing a different-but-equally-valid edit should not be penalized
The eval should distinguish editorially skilled but stylistically divergent from simply careless
task_context: The eval scoring module uses 6 dimensions to judge a model's line-edit against a human editor reference on a 1-10 scale. The product's editorial identity is defined by 7 pillars but these are not directly used as eval dimensions.
